title: Compact Handoff Guidelets + Postmortem Shortcuts for Alert Composer
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Introduce compact, contextual handoff guidelets and one-click postmortem shortcuts inside the Alert Composer to reduce noisy on-call transitions and speed incident closure.
description: Problem: On-call engineers repeatedly lose context during alert handoffs and spend time hunting for postmortem templates, playbooks, and previous incident links. The current Alert Composer can attach runbooks and slack channels but lacks in-situ micro-guides that surface who to contact, past related incidents, and a fast path to create a postmortem link.
goals: Design a compact guidelet pattern that appears in the Composer and Handoff drawer to surface: primary on-call, escalation path, recent related incidents (3), and a postmortem quick-link.
Provide a single-click 'Create Postmortem' shortcut that pre-fills metadata and links back to the alert and timeline.
Keep the UI low-friction for paging and mobile narrow widths.
Define analytics events for handoff accepts/declines and postmortem creation so PM can measure reduction in handoff churn.
out_of_scope: Full-fledged postmortem editor (we will deep-link to existing doc templates)
Automatic root-cause suggestion from traces/logs—this is for a later cycle
acceptance_criteria: Guidelet appears in Alert Composer for alerts with SLO breach=true and severity>=P2.
Handoff drawer shows: primary on-call (name + role), escalation contacts (2), three recent related incidents with timestamps and short titles.
Create Postmortem opens modal with pre-filled alert ID, timestamps, and one-click create that returns a postmortem URL.
Telemetry: events emitted -> alert.handoff.open, alert.handoff.accept, alert.handoff.decline, postmortem.create_success, postmortem.create_fail.
UX works at 320px width (mobile) and passes accessibility contrast and keyboard flows.
Engineering smoke test: end-to-end link created, back-link from postmortem to alert, and analytics visible in console dashboard.
decisions: Use a compact 'guidelet' card (max height 160px) instead of full panels to keep composer vertical space minimal.
Limit related incidents to 3, sorted by relevance (shared affected model or same alert rule), to reduce cognitive load.
Implement postmortem creation as a shallow API call that creates a doc shell in the company docs system and returns a short URL—no editor embedded in V1.
tradeoffs: Compact guidelet reduces context but avoids overwhelming the composer — follow-ups will add expandable details.
One-click postmortem creation limits metadata capture initially; we prioritize speed over completeness for v1.
Linking to external doc storage keeps backend surface small but requires auth SSO checks; engineering must handle 401 gracefully.
